key_path: Sign up at linear.app with Google OAuth (or email magic link/code)
Create workspace (name + URL slug) during onboarding
Settings > Account > Security & access > Personal API keys > New key (optionally read-only / team-scoped)
human_gates_notes: Email gate disappears with Google OAuth (then it is an OAuth consent click). No card, no phone. In existing workspaces admins can restrict member API key creation.

agent_native_auth.cli_device_login: no (no official general CLI; only the CLI importer)
agent_native_auth.personal_access_tokens: yes - personal API keys, can be limited to read-only
agent_native_auth.scoped_tokens: yes - read/write scopes on keys and OAuth (read, write, issues:create, admin, plus actor=app)
agent_native_auth.management_api_mints_keys: no public key-minting API; OAuth app manifests exist for app creation

remote.auth: OAuth 2.1 with DCR, OR Authorization: Bearer <Linear API key>

mcp.local: none official (use npx mcp-remote for stdio-only clients)
mcp.one_click_install: Cursor deeplink on docs page; Claude connectors directory; VS Code via MCP: Add Server

docs_for_agents.openapi: n/a - GraphQL schema (introspection + public schema on GitHub)

score_justification: Google-OAuth signup, one-screen API key, and an MCP server that takes both OAuth-DCR and a plain API key bearer; read-only MCP URL is a nice safety rail.
best_practice: MCP accepts the same personal API key as a bearer header (plus a dedicated /mcp/readonly endpoint), so headless agents never need a browser OAuth dance.
biggest_gap: No official CLI with device login and no llms-full.txt; API key creation still requires clicking through the web settings UI.
